title: Direct cDNA Synthesis
author: Yao Xiao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6knhcve
materials: Laboratory Procedures, PJ Hansen Laboratory - University of Florida 1 | cDNA synthesis and pre-amplification for single blastocyst RT-PCR Direct cDNA synthesis and pre-amplifcation of single embryos for RT-PCR Yao Xiao and Peter J Hansen Department of Animal Sciences, University of Florida Introduction This protocol allows gene expression analysis within single embryos on multiple targets in either conventional real-time PCR or using the Fluidigm pla tform. The protocol makes extensive use of the CellsDirect Kit from ThermoFisher Scientific (catalog number 11753). References to the kit refer to this product. This protocol describes a method that converts RNA directly into cDNA without RNA extraction, which avoids the variation due to extraction process. The number of genes of interest can be up to more than 100. However, the target genes for analysis have to be determined prior to cDNA synthesis. Once the cDNA is made, there is no way to add additional gene to analyze. The best approach to primer design is to have primers span an intron in the target region. This is not a requirement, however, because of the DNase treatment included in the protocol. Embryo collection and storage 1. Prepare capillary tube for embr yo collection: place a capillary tube (5-000-1005, Drummond) in the flame of an alcohol or Bunsen burner. Heat until the glass becomes soft and then pull. Use a mini grinding disc to cut the tube where the outer diameter is around 300 μm. Use this capillary tube for transferring embryos into collection tubes to minimize the amount of solution that introduced. 2. Prepare collection tubes: add 1 μl of resuspension buffer (provided in the kit) into each RNAase-free PCR tube. 3. Wash embryos with DEPC-t reated Dulbecco’s phosphate buffered saline containing 0.2% (w/v) polyvinylpyrrolidone (DPBS-PVP) three times. 4. Remove zona with Acid Tyrode’s (T1788, Sigma).

steps.title: Repeat step 3
steps.instruction: Perform step 3 again as described earlier in the protocol.

steps.title: Collect embryos and freeze
steps.instruction: Collect each embryo into a collection tube using a pulled glass capillary tube prepared above to avoid introducing excess solution that would dilute the buffer. Immediately snap‑freeze the tube in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Store embryos at –80°C
steps.instruction: Place each frozen embryo tube at –80 °C for storage.

steps.title: Add lysis enhancer
steps.instruction: Withdraw samples from the –80 °C freezer, keep on ice, and add 0.5 µl of lysis enhancer (provided in the kit) to each tube under a stereomicroscope, taking care that the embryo does not stick to the pipette tip.

steps.title: Lyse embryos at 70°C
steps.instruction: Lyse embryos by incubating at 70 °C for 20 min in a PCR machine. After 10 min pause the program, tap the tube to mix, then resume incubation for the remaining 10 min.

steps.title: Add DNase I and buffer
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 µl of DNase I (1 U/µl; 1 U digests 1 µg DNA at 37 °C) and 0.22 µl of DNase I buffer (from the kit) to each tube. Mix by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Digest DNA at 25°C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 25 °C for 15 min in a PCR machine.

steps.title: Add EDTA and mix
steps.instruction: Add 0.55 µl of 25 mM EDTA (from the kit), vortex briefly to mix, then spin down briefly in a microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Deactivate DNase I
steps.instruction: Heat the tubes at 70 °C for 10 min in a PCR machine to deactivate DNase I. The total volume should now be approximately 2.75 µl.

steps.title: Prepare 500 nM primer mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a primer mix containing 500 nM of each primer. Example for 100 µM stock primers: (i) make a 10 µM intermediate mix by adding 10 µl forward + 10 µl reverse + 80 µl nuclease‑free water (total 100 µl). (ii) For the final mix, add 5 µl of each 10 µM gene‑specific primer (A, B, C, …) to nuclease‑free water to a final volume of 100 µl. If mixing >20 genes, add 0.5 µl of each 100 µM stock and bring the volume to 100 µl. For a 96‑primer Deltagene assay (100 µM primers from Fluidigm), add 1 µl of each primer to 104 µl water to obtain 200 µl of primer mix.

steps.title: Prepare cDNA master mix
steps.instruction: For each reaction assemble a 7.5 µl master mix as follows: 5 µl CellsDirect 2X reaction mix (kit), 0.5 µl SuperScript III RT/Platinum Taq mix (kit), 1 µl primer mix (500 nM), 1 µl DNA suspension buffer (T0220, Teknova). Add 7.5 µl of this master mix to each tube containing the lysed embryo.

steps.title: Run reverse‑transcription PCR
steps.instruction: Program the PCR machine: 1) 50 °C for 20 min (reverse transcription); 2) 95 °C for 2 min; 3) 18 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s followed by 60 °C for 4 min.

steps.title: Prepare Exonuclease I mix
steps.instruction: Per sample, prepare a master mix of 0.8 µl 20 U/µl Exonuclease I, 0.4 µl Exonuclease I buffer, and 2.8 µl nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Exonuclease I digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min, then heat at 80 °C for 15 min, and finally hold at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Dilute cDNA 1:5
steps.instruction: The cDNA volume after the previous step is 14 µl. Add 56 µl nuclease‑free water to achieve a 1:5 dilution (total 70 µl). Store the diluted cDNA at –20 °C. This amount is sufficient for 28 genes by conventional real‑time PCR or 96 genes on a Fluidigm platform; if needed, dilute further up to 1:10.

steps.title: Prepare EvaGreen qPCR mix
steps.instruction: For each qPCR reaction combine: 10.4 µl EvaGreen (catalog 1725211, Bio‑Rad), 1.26 µl 10 µM forward and reverse primer mix, 7.1 µl nuclease‑free water, and 1.2 µl cDNA. Use 1.2 µl RNase/DNase‑free water as a no‑template control.

steps.title: Run real‑time PCR program
steps.instruction: Run the following cycling program: 95 °C for 30 s, then 95 °C for 5 s, then 60 °C for 5 s with plate read. Repeat the 60 °C step (step 2) for an additional 30 cycles. After amplification, perform a melt‑curve: increase temperature from 65 °C to 95 °C in 0.5 °C increments, hold 5 s at each step, and read the plate.
